rationale:
Evidence from iteration 1 (score 556.7, up from 317.4). The oval now finishes in 100% of trials (mean 2.03 s, max_error 0.025). The s-bend finishes in 45% of trials and the slalom in 0%. Slalom runs end off track at progress 0.30, with max_error 0.064, just over the 0.06 m limit, and 1.15 line-loss events per run. So the remaining failure is still at sharp bends, and the robot leaves the tape there.

Change: lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.2 and keep kp 3.5, kd 0.6, ki 0 and the geometry unchanged. This follows the Evaluator's requested change. The aim is to cut the centripetal and slip error that pushes the robot past 0.06 m on the tight arcs, and to reduce line loss when the tape drifts out from under the sensors. I expect the s-bend completion rate to rise and the slalom to start completing some runs. The oval should still finish in about 2.2 s (2.03 × 1.3/1.2), well under the 3.0 s limit, so the time term loses only a little.

Risks: the average speed may fall too low for the 3 s limit on the longer tracks. If the oval completion time goes above about 2.5 s, or the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06, the next step is to raise kp to about 3.8 with kd 0.7, to test whether more steering authority is the limit rather than speed. Geometry is held fixed so this speed effect is isolated.

Hypotheses: (a) the slalom failure is partly speed-driven, so progress on the slalom rises above 0.30; (b) line_loss_events drop below 1.0 on the bends; (c) steering_oscillation stays near 0.3 or lower.
